newsitem.title: USA: MBL Life Assurance settles creditor litigation.
newsitem.headline: MBL Life Assurance settles creditor litigation.

text.p: MBL Life Assurance Corp said Thursday it reached a settlement among parties involved in appealing the Mutual Benefit Life Insurance Co rehabilitation plan and other litigation over to policyholder interest crediting rates.
Mutual Benefit Life failed in 1991 and was taken over by the N.J. state insurance commissioner.

Over the next several years, there were extended negotiations between the company, the state guarantee associations and different life insurance companies to put together a rehabilitation plan and protect policy holders.

MBL said it settled the contested issue of who owned Mutual Benefit at the end of the rehabilitation period in 1999, granting to the insurance company's unsecured creditors 70 percent ownership and to policy holders 30 percent.

The initial rehabilitation plan had granted policy holders, who pay a fee which goes down each year when withdrawing money from the company, 100 percent ownership at the end of the rehabilitation period, MBL said.
The court amended this plan, granting creditors 100 percent ownership, MBL said. The amendment was appealed and litigation had been going on since 1993, MBL said.
The liabilities and most assets of Mutual Benefit Life were transferred to MBL after the rehabilitation plan went into effect in 1994, the company said.
The company said as part of the settlement, all litigation was dropped without prejudice.
MBL said it also settled the issue of interest credited to policy holders on their accounts.
Policy holders pay to withdraw money from Mutual Benefit, but the company credits interest to their accounts. Mutual Benefit's creditors had contested these payments, MBL said.
But under the settlement, the crediting rate was fixed until the end of the rehabilitation period at 1996 rates between 4.35 percent and 5.35 percent, MBL said.
